description: A completely different user. Different names, different domain, no seed. Does the mechanism generalise, or was it tuned to one persona?
rationale: Neither correction contained 'mira'. The claim was never about Aaditya specifically; it is about phonetic identity, and this shows the same generalisation for a name the system was built without.

description: A third spelling of the same new name.
rationale: ee, i and ei all reduce to the same vowel, so one correction covers a family of spellings for this user exactly as it did for the other.

rationale: The guard is not a list of exceptions for 'kiwi'. It is a rule about ordinary words lacking contextual support, and it holds for a homophone that did not exist when the rule was written.

description: The same word, same user, supported by context this time.

rationale: 'design' and 'system' were mined from this user's own sentences, not from a list anyone wrote. Paired with the case above, this is the whole product in two lines for a persona the system never saw.

description: Nothing is hardcoded. The seeded persona's memories must not exist for a different user.
asr: ask aditya to review the sarvam kiwi service
formatted: Ask Aditya to review the Sarvam Kiwi service.
expected: Ask Aditya to review the Sarvam Kiwi service.
rationale: The brief's own example, run against a user who never taught those words. Everything the system does for the seeded persona comes from that persona's observations; none of it is in the code. If any of this repository's behaviour were special-cased to Aaditya or Kivi, this case would catch it.
